paras: The lynching of Lawrence was the hanging of a Black man accused of rape by a "company of men" within the limits of Girard, Kansas, some time before mid-August 1885. It drew notice because a mass meeting of citizens of nearby Baxter Springs adopted resolutions formally approving the hanging and thanking those who carried it out.

The surviving coverage gives no date, account of the hanging itself, or details of the accusation beyond The Clarion's statement that the man was lynched "for the atrocious and unpardonable crime of rape." According to the resolutions, the hanging was the work of a "company" whose members were identified only as "A. B. C. D. and others," who had acted "bravely and at their own peril." The company also damaged property in Girard, though the resolutions do not say what was damaged.

At a mass meeting, the citizens of Baxter Springs resolved that they approved "of the hanging of Lawrence" and thanked the company for accomplishing "that which we all desired should be done." A second resolution expressed regret to the people of Girard that the "termination of a detestable criminal's life" had occurred within their town and hoped their community would never be "agitated and outraged" by a similar crime. The meeting asked that claims for property damage done by the "company of men" in Girard be sent to the "citizens committee" of Baxter Springs for adjustment.
No report of an inquest, arrest, or prosecution appears in the coverage.

The only report found ran in The Clarion of Jackson, Mississippi, on August 19, 1885, under the headline "Kansas Formally Applauding the Lynchers." The paper said it had "recently" published an account of the lynching and now had "the satisfaction to note" that a neighboring town had thanked "the lynchers for their speedy administration of justice to the criminal." The resolutions themselves never mention Lawrence's race; that identification comes from The Clarion's introduction, which called him "a negro."
No coverage of the hanging appears in the Black press, and The Clarion's earlier account of the lynching has not been located.

accounts.label: Baxter Springs mass-meeting resolutions
accounts.gist: The citizens approved the hanging of Lawrence, thanked the company that carried it out, regretted that it happened in Girard, and offered to settle claims for property damage there.

accounts.label: The Clarion's comment
accounts.gist: The Jackson paper said it had earlier reported the lynching of a Black man in Kansas for rape and welcomed the resolutions as thanks for the "speedy administration of justice."

framing.detail: Headline "Kansas Formally Applauding the Lynchers"; the paper notes the resolutions with "satisfaction" and calls rape an "atrocious and unpardonable crime."
